events.title: Gore carries California
events.text: Al Gore carried California by almost twelve points; it has voted Democratic for president since 1992.

events.title: Davis re-elected
events.text: Governor Gray Davis, a Democrat, beat Bill Simon by five points.

events.title: The recall
events.text: Voters recalled Governor Davis and elected Arnold Schwarzenegger, a Republican, in his place.

events.title: Bush loses California
events.text: George W. Bush lost California by ten points as he won a second term nationally.

events.title: Schwarzenegger re-elected
events.text: Schwarzenegger won a second term by seventeen points.

events.title: Obama by 24
events.text: Barack Obama carried California by twenty-four points.

events.title: Top-two primary
events.text: Voters approved Proposition 14: one primary ballot for all, with the top two advancing whatever their party.

events.title: Brown returns
events.text: Jerry Brown, governor from 1975 to 1983, beat Meg Whitman by thirteen points.

events.title: Hilton moves west
events.text: Steve Hilton, a former strategy director to Britain's prime minister, moved to Stanford, in Silicon Valley.

events.title: First top-two race
events.text: In the first top-two race for governor, Brown beat Neel Kashkari, a Republican, sixty to forty.

events.title: Clinton by 30
events.text: Hillary Clinton carried California by thirty points.

events.title: Attorney General Becerra
events.text: Xavier Becerra, a congressman since 1993, became California's attorney general.

events.title: The Next Revolution
events.text: Hilton began hosting a weekly Fox News programme, which ran until 2023.

events.title: Newsom elected
events.text: Gavin Newsom beat John Cox, a Republican, sixty-two to thirty-eight.

events.title: Becerra elected
events.text: Becerra won a full term as attorney general.

events.title: Biden by 29
events.text: Joe Biden carried California by twenty-nine points.

events.title: Secretary Becerra
events.text: On 18 March the U.S. Senate confirmed Becerra as Secretary of Health and Human Services, 50 to 49.

events.title: Hilton a citizen
events.text: On 11 May Hilton became a U.S. citizen at a ceremony in San Francisco.

events.title: Recall fails
events.text: Sixty-two percent voted No in a recall election, and Governor Newsom stayed in office.

events.title: Newsom re-elected
events.text: Newsom beat Brian Dahle, a Republican state senator, by eighteen points.

events.title: Golden Together
events.text: Hilton founded Golden Together, a California policy group, as his Fox programme ended.

events.title: Ten counties flip
events.text: Donald Trump carried ten counties that had voted for Joe Biden, among them Riverside, San Bernardino and Fresno.

events.title: Imperial turns
events.text: Imperial County, on the Mexican border, voted Republican for president by under a point.

events.title: Harris by 20
events.text: Kamala Harris carried her home state by twenty points, down from Biden's twenty-nine.

events.title: Becerra enters
events.text: On 2 April Becerra announced his run: “The California Dream is slipping away.”

events.title: Hilton launches
events.text: On 22 April Hilton launched his campaign in Huntington Beach.

events.title: Proposition 50
events.text: In November voters approved Proposition 50, redrawing California's congressional districts until 2030.

events.title: Former aide indicted
events.text: Newsom's former chief of staff was indicted over money taken from Becerra's dormant campaign account; Becerra was not charged.

events.title: Trump endorses Hilton
events.text: In April President Trump endorsed Hilton.

events.title: No party endorsement
events.text: At its San Diego convention the state Republican Party endorsed no one: Chad Bianco 49 percent, Hilton 44.

events.title: A guilty plea
events.text: In May the former Newsom aide pleaded guilty and agreed to repay Becerra's account $225,000.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 2 June Becerra (28.0 percent) and Hilton (24.6) finished first and second among 61 candidates.

events.title: Steyer third
events.text: Tom Steyer, a Democrat, won 22.8 percent, third, and conceded.

events.title: Hilton's counties
events.text: Hilton led the primary in thirty-four of the fifty-eight counties, most of them inland.

events.title: Newsom endorses Becerra
events.text: On 9 June Governor Newsom endorsed Becerra.

events.title: Bianco declines
events.text: On 15 July Sheriff Chad Bianco said he would not, “at this point”, endorse Hilton.

events.title: At the speedway
events.text: On 25 September Hilton campaigned at the Madera Speedway.

events.title: The debate
events.text: On 30 September Becerra and Hilton met in a CNN debate.

events.title: Ballots go out
events.text: From 5 October every active registered voter is mailed a ballot.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Californians choose between Becerra and Hilton.

eras: The top-two primary and Brown's return
chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; certified state results). It is a simplification: California chooses its governor in its own race, and its voters have elected Republican governors within living memory (most recently in 2003 and 2006), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes: about a quarter of California's votes are cast in Los Angeles County alone. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on California, so outer states are cut at the edge.
